title: Reconstruct why a consequential action was allowed without model recollection
narrative: An auditor can rebuild a review from the saved decision log and trace alone: which recipe ran, what the policy decided and under which revision, how trusted the source was, what scope was delegated, why something was denied, who approved it, and which side effects actually happened. When any of that is missing the record says exactly which part, instead of relying on what the model remembers. Related: `taloneth_policy_replay`, `nubble_insp_trace_reconciliation`. Tracks MH-DOTS-09[^insp-dots-09].
implementation: `ReviewAuditRecord` in `review_audit.py` composes `DecisionRecord` and `TraceEnvelope` (recipe id and version, `policy_version` / `policy_revision`, approval, denial, and effect ids, freshness summary) with caller-attested source trust, delegated scope, and denial reasons. `from_records()` prefers the decision over the envelope on overlap; `missing_dimensions()` and `reconstructable()` name gaps (denials need reasons and ids, human-approved verdicts need approval ids, executed actions need effect ids).
validation: Harness `cli` `probe` loads `plans/review_audit_reconstruct.yaml` (human-readable probe plan); hard expects on declared observation keys.
